text:
priya (ML Eng): quick sync — proposing a small, opinionated nightly sanity gate for quantized bring-up. want a really tight fast-fail so we don't waste dev cycles.
noah (ML Eng): +1. what metrics are you thinking?
priya (ML Eng): core idea: run the mini-harness overnight on canary models and fail the build if any of these happen:
- perplexity increase > 3% on eval corpus A
- L1 embedding drift > 0.07 (cos sim drop)
- `safety` classifier false positives increase > 1.5x baseline
noah (ML Eng): makes sense. include absolute floors too (e.g., if baseline perf is already bad we shouldn't block).
derek (PM): heads-up — if nightly fails it should auto-open a ticket and ping the model owner. otherwise we'll miss regressions.
priya (ML Eng): yes — plan: fail -> create GH issue via eval-bot -> post to #eng-ml with summary and link to full harness run. low-noise policy: only escalate on >2 metrics triggered or a single catastrophic metric.
sam (SRE): careful with noisy thresholds causing CI churn overnight. can we add a transient buffer: require failures persist for 2 consecutive nights before org-wide alert?
priya (ML Eng): good call. proposal: nightly quick-fail gates: immediate GH issue + owner ping. org-wide alert (pager or #incidents) only if same model fails 2 nights in a row.
eval-bot: nightly-run finished for model: gpt-small-quant v2 — results: perplexity delta +3.6%, emb cos sim -0.081, safety FP +0.5x. Gate: FAILED (perplexity and emb heuristics crossed). Link: https://eval.internal/runs/2376543210
noah (ML Eng): hitting +3.6% is right at our proposed 3% threshold — we should record per-prompt breakdown to see if it's concentrated.
priya (ML Eng): agreed. adding a `breakdown` artifact that includes top-20 prompts triggering delta, sample responses, and token-level diffs. example config below:```yaml
nightly_gate:
  thresholds:
    perplexity_pct: 3.0
    embedding_cos_drop: 0.07
    safety_fp_mult: 1.5
  consecutive_failures_for_alert: 2
  owner_notify: true
  create_issue_on_fail: true
  artifacts:
    - breakdown.json
    - diffs.tar.gz
    - sample_responses.json
```
noah (ML Eng): looks good. can we also log the quantization config used (bits, backend, per-channel vs per-tensor) so triage is faster?
priya (ML Eng): yes — will make that required metadata in the run. also include inference config (batching, KV cache warmup length).
derek (PM): operational question — what is the run budget? we can't have full eval on every candidate. keep it to ~1k prompts and 10 stress seeds.
priya (ML Eng): agreed. mini-harness: 1k curated prompts (mix of synth/real), 10 random seeds for sampling metrics, and 3 stress lengths (32, 512, 2048). should fit in nightly window.
sam (SRE): please add a job-time cap and resource tag so it doesn't stomp production infra. also mark retry policy: no retries for failed runs (we want deterministic history).
priya (ML Eng): noted. final checklist for implementing gate: 1) threshold config in repo (yaml) 2) nightly job in CI with resource tags 3) eval-bot creates issue + posts summary 4) breakdown artifacts uploaded to bucket 5) alert on 2-night persistence.
eval-bot: created issue #ML-quant-489: "gpt-small-quant v2 — nightly gate failure" and posted summary to #eng-ml.
noah (ML Eng): will take a first-pass on triage in the morning, focusing on prompt breakdown.
derek (PM): solid. if triage shows single-prompt skew, we can un-block with an owner note and continue. otherwise follow rollback / revert plan.
priya (ML Eng): thanks — I'll open a PR with the yaml and CI job, pinging owners in the PR. :thumbsup:
